Drop.NotAChallenge: Only challenges can go in the Subsystems tab.
Drop.ChallengeInJournal: Challenges stay in the Subsystems tab.
Drop.NormalFolder: Only challenge folders can go in the Subsystems tab.
Drop.ChallengeFolder: Challenge folders stay in the Subsystems tab.

Panel.Replaced: {name} left the panel. It is still running; right-click it in the Subsystems tab and choose Show on panel to bring it back.
Panel.PositionHint: Where the challenge panel starts at the top of the screen. Anyone can drag it by its header to a spot of their own.
Panel.NoCharacter: You need an assigned character to roll. Ask the GM to assign one.
Panel.NoGMActor: Select a token, or pick a PC under Roll as in the challenge window.
Panel.SkillGone: That check is no longer available.

Challenge.Label: Challenge
Challenge.Name: Name
Challenge.ActedSet: Click to mark as acted this round
Challenge.ActedClear: Acted this round. Click to clear.
Challenge.CurrentRoundLocked: Current round. While the challenge runs, change it with the previous and next round buttons.
Challenge.MaximumRoundsHint: Blank: rounds with no limit. 0: no rounds at all, for a challenge that lasts a campaign, such as Reputation. The panel hides the round, and the sheet disables its round buttons. Neither shows acted marks.
Challenge.EntryGone: That was deleted, so the changes were not saved.
Challenge.ModifierGone: That entry was deleted, so the changes were not saved.
Challenge.RollBonusHint: Added to the roll as a PF2e modifier of this type, so PF2e's stacking rules apply. Below 0 for a penalty. It applies to the same checks as the DC change.
Challenge.EveryCheckHint: The DC change and roll bonus apply to every check, including checks and actions added later. The lists below are ignored while this is on.
Challenge.EndConfirm: End this challenge? The panel closes for everyone. The final state stays on the sheet.
Challenge.ResetConfirm: Return this challenge to unspent? Points, counters, rounds and reveals go back to how they were at Start.
Challenge.NotActiveGM: Another GM is running this challenge. Only the active GM can change it.
Challenge.DropActorHint: Drag an NPC or character from the Actors sidebar onto this window to add it to this challenge.
Challenge.ParticipantWorldOnly: Only an actor in the Actors sidebar can join a challenge. Import a compendium actor first.
Challenge.ParticipantType: {name} can't join a challenge: only characters and NPCs can roll its checks.
Challenge.NoPCSelected: Choose a PC to roll for.
Challenge.RollSkill: Roll {skill}, DC {dc}, for the chosen PC
Challenge.Subject: Subject
Challenge.SecretHint: Rolled as a secret check, like Recall Knowledge.
Challenge.ThresholdDcHint: Applies while the threshold is reached: to this subject's checks, or to every check for a counter's threshold.
Challenge.PerRoundHint: Added when the round advances. Previous round takes it back.
Challenge.ChallengeModifiersHint: Entries for the whole challenge. A DC change applies to every check with the chosen skills, on any subject.
Challenge.LevelHint: Optional. New checks start at this level's DC, and the action window's difficulty buttons set DCs from it. A new level moves every check that has a difficulty.
Challenge.LevelDcText: Level {level}: DC {dc}. A difficulty button sets a check's DC from it. A typed DC stays as typed; a faint button marks the difficulty it equals.
Challenge.DifficultyNeedsLevel: Give the subject a level to set DCs by difficulty.
Challenge.ActionsHint: The DC change and roll bonus apply only to checks of the ticked actions, including checks added to them later. Other actions are untouched. With skills ticked under Checks too, only those skills' checks in these actions count.
Challenge.ChallengeActionsHint: The DC change and roll bonus apply only to checks of the ticked actions, on every subject with an action of that name. Other actions are untouched. With skills ticked under Checks too, only those skills' checks in these actions count.
Challenge.ChecksHint: The DC change and roll bonus apply only to checks of the ticked skills, in any of this subject's actions. Other skills are untouched. With actions ticked too, only checks in those actions count.
Challenge.ChallengeChecksHint: The DC change and roll bonus apply only to checks of the ticked skills, on any subject. Other skills are untouched. With actions ticked too, only checks in those actions count.
Challenge.TrackLimits: A minimum is above its maximum, so that value was not limited.
Challenge.ReachedFollows: Reached follows the value on a track that counts both ways.
Challenge.ShowThresholdListHint: Off: the panel lists no thresholds under the counter. The marks on its display follow their own checkbox.
Challenge.ShowThresholdMarksHint: Off: revealed thresholds leave no mark on the counter's bar, steps or track. The list under it follows its own checkbox.
Challenge.PerPcHint: One value for each party PC. A roll changes the roller's value; a modifier changes everyone's. No thresholds or change each round.
Challenge.PcNoteHint: GM only. For example: 1 dud (forged papers), 1 only for paperwork.
Challenge.MultipleSubjectsHint: On: any number of subjects can be revealed at once, and the panel shows each revealed one. Off: revealing a subject hides every other subject, so players see one at a time. Use off for subjects taken in order, such as a chase's obstacles: revealing the next one moves the panel on in one click. Hiding a subject never reveals another.
Challenge.DisplayHint: How players see this counter on the panel once it is revealed. Auto: a bar if it has thresholds or counts both ways, else a number. Steps: filled segments, like the round counter. Track: a marker that moves along a row of slots. Steps and Track need a maximum and show as a bar without one.

SSM.ChoosePresetHint: Pick a starting template. Everything can be edited afterwards.

GmNotes.Obstacles: Obstacles: add one obstacle per barrier between the party and its goal. Set each obstacle's Infiltration Points maximum to the points it needs, and give its Overcome action one check row per way past it, each with its DC. For an individual obstacle, which each PC overcomes alone, turn on Per PC on its counter. For several objectives in sequence, give each objective's obstacles their own category, such as Objective 2, and reveal the next objective's obstacles when the first PC moves on. The first obstacle starts revealed and later ones hidden: reveal each when the party reaches it. Rolls change nothing, so after each roll use + and − on the obstacle's points, and mark it Complete when it's cleared.
GmNotes.Awareness: Awareness Points: Next round adds 1. Add more by hand with + when the party's actions raise the alarm. Its thresholds mark the preset tiers and change DCs while reached; edit them to fit the site. You get a notice when one is reached.
GmNotes.Edge: Edge Points: one per PC. Add them with + on each PC's row, or type in what the PCs earned in an Infiltration Preparation challenge. When a PC spends one on a failed check, lower their value with − and give the points a success would. Each PC's row has a note for anything only you should know about their points.
GmNotes.Complication: Complication: add an obstacle and set its Category to Complication. Remove its Infiltration Points counter, and leave it hidden until its trigger happens. When a failure adds Awareness Points, add them with the Awareness + button. A lasting penalty is a modifier you turn on.
GmNotes.Opportunity: Opportunity that needs a roll: add an obstacle, set its Category to Opportunity, remove its counter and rename its action Attempt. One with no roll is a one-time challenge modifier in the Opportunity category instead.

5.Name: Suspicions are raised
5.Description: Obstacle DCs +1. The first time the PCs reach this tier, a complication occurs: reveal one.

10.Name: Something goes wrong
10.Description: The first time the PCs reach this tier, a complication occurs: reveal one.

15.Name: The opposition is on alert
15.Description: With the 5 AP tier, obstacle DCs are +2 in total. The first time the PCs reach this tier, a complication occurs: reveal one.

BribeContact.Name: Bribe Contact
BribeContact.Description: Requires a contact (Gain Contact). The bribe is worth at least one-tenth of the Currency per additional PC (Table 10-9); doubling it grants a +2 circumstance bonus. DC: hard or very hard.

GainContact.Name: Gain Contact
GainContact.Description: A Lore suited to the contact also works. DC: normal, hard or very hard.

Gossip.Name: Gossip
Gossip.Description: DC: normal, hard or very hard.

ScoutLocation.Name: Scout Location
ScoutLocation.Description: DC: normal, hard or very hard.

SecureDisguises.Name: Secure Disguises
SecureDisguises.Description: DC: normal, hard or very hard.

GmNotes.Intro: Run this challenge before the infiltration, as its own challenge with its own rounds. Each preparation activity is an action on the Preparation subject; players roll them from the panel. Add or remove activities and check rows to fit the adventure.
GmNotes.Points: Rolls change nothing: after each roll, add Edge Points on that PC's row and Awareness Points with +. Awareness is hidden from players; reveal it with its eye if you want them to see it.
GmNotes.Notes: A dud or cursed Edge Point still goes on the counter, as the PC thinks it worked. Write which point it is in that PC's note on the Edge Points row, along with any point that only works in one situation.
GmNotes.Handover: When preparation ends, type each PC's Edge Points and the Awareness Points into the infiltration challenge.

GmNotes.Obstacles: Obstacles: add one obstacle per stage of the chase, in the order the party meets them. Set each obstacle's Chase Points maximum to the points it needs. Give its Overcome action one check row per way past it, each with its DC. The first obstacle starts revealed and the rest hidden; Allow multiple subjects is off, so revealing the next obstacle hides the last one.
GmNotes.Tracks: Tracks: Party and Quarry hold each side's obstacle number. Set both maximums to the number of obstacles, and each value to where that side starts. Rename Quarry to fit the chase, such as Pursuers or Rival. Quarry moves +1 each round: change its amount each round, or nudge it with + and −, for a different pace. For a race against time, hide Quarry and set Maximum Rounds.
GmNotes.Running: Each round: rolls change nothing, so after each roll use + and − on the obstacle's Chase Points. When the party clears an obstacle, add 1 to Party and reveal the next obstacle. Next round moves Quarry. When a side gets past the last obstacle, mark that obstacle Complete.
GmNotes.Variants: Variants: for split paths, give each path's obstacles a category named for the path, and turn on Allow multiple subjects while the party chooses. If the PCs split up, set Party to Per PC, so each PC has an obstacle number, and turn on Allow multiple subjects so each PC's obstacle shows.

GmNotes.Factions: Factions: add one faction per group the party deals with, such as a guild, church or village. Each faction has a Reputation Points counter from −50 to +50, with GM Core's tiers as thresholds. A faction starts at 0, Ignored; set the value higher or lower if the party is already known to that group. A new faction starts revealed: hide one the party hasn't met yet. Factions have no actions, since nothing is rolled.
GmNotes.Changing: Favors and disservices: use + and − on the faction's counter, on the sheet or the panel. Each tier's GM text says which favors and disservices still count at that tier. Tiers tick and untick themselves as the value moves, so the highest ticked tier is where the party stands. With no tier ticked, the party is Ignored.
GmNotes.Running: Across sessions: reputation lasts the whole campaign. Start the challenge once and leave it running; there are no rounds, so Maximum Rounds is 0 and the sheet and panel show no round. Show it on the panel when the party should see where they stand. For a long list, turn off Show thresholds list on panel on a faction's counter: its bar keeps a tick per tier.

30.Name: Revered
30.Description: Only major favors add points. Only moderate and major disservices take points away.

15.Name: Admired
15.Description: Only major favors add points. Any disservice takes points away.

5.Name: Liked
5.Description: Only moderate and major favors add points. Any disservice takes points away.

-5.Name: Disliked
-5.Description: Any favor adds points. Only moderate and major disservices take points away.

-15.Name: Hated
-15.Description: Any favor adds points. Only major disservices take points away.

-30.Name: Hunted
-30.Description: Only moderate and major favors add points. Only major disservices take points away.

GmNotes.Library: Library areas: add one area per research check in the stat block, such as a shelf, a room or an NPC to question. Give its Research action one check row per skill, each with its DC. Set the area's RP Gathered maximum to its Maximum RP. Areas start revealed, as the party chooses where to research: hide any they haven't found yet.
GmNotes.Rolling: Each roll: rolls change nothing, so after a success use + on the area's RP Gathered and on Research Points, once per RP gained. When RP Gathered is full, the area gives no more: mark it Complete. On a critical failure use − on Research Points only, and write the false discovery in a secret block in the area's description, which players don't see.
GmNotes.Thresholds: Thresholds: add the stat block's research thresholds to Research Points, fewest RP first, with what the party learns as player text. Thresholds tick as the points rise, and the GM gets a notice on each one. To change the library when a threshold is reached, such as a new check or a harder DC, edit the area.
GmNotes.Time: Time: set the round length with the players, from 10 minutes to a day, and set Maximum Rounds to the time limit. Days goes up by 1 each round; rename it, such as to Hours, if rounds are shorter. Add each timed event as a threshold on Days: it starts hidden, so reveal it when it happens.
